Implement this feature in the repository. Inspect and edit repository files. Do not use the network, other repository directories, additional agents, or outside feedback. Do not modify tests to conceal failures. Do not commit changes. Do not run tests, scripts, or any repository code, and do not install packages; work by reading and editing files. 

SPECIFICATION:
## Goals
- Add Progress column TimeElapsedColumn showing a task's running time as hours:minutes:seconds, truncated to whole seconds.
- When a task reaches its total, freeze its displayed value at the elapsed time recorded then.
- Keep the placeholder and duration format consistent with TimeRemainingColumn.
- Add a __rich__ method to the palette class so the palette renders as a table.
## Scope
In scope:
- The new column in the progress module, next to TimeRemainingColumn.
- A finished-time value on each task, captured by Progress update and advance, cleared by Progress reset and the task's internal reset.
- Deriving a task's finished state from that value.
- A default style entry, Palette.__rich__ with its tests, and a changelog entry.
Out of scope:
- Signature changes to public methods, new dependencies, new clocks, new public Progress methods.
- Unrelated edits such as exception chaining, comment cleanups, the version bump, and demo wiring.
## Terminology
- elapsed: the task's existing elapsed value. Absent if the task has not started; otherwise the current time (or the stop time if stopped) minus the start time. Time comes from the existing clock; no new time source is added.
- finished time: the elapsed value recorded by a capture. Absent until captured. Zero is valid; "present" means not absent.
- capture: storing the finished time under the Workflows rules. Clear: setting it back to absent.
- finished: true if and only if a finished time is present.
## Workflows
1. Rendering. When TimeElapsedColumn renders a task:
   - If the task is finished, show its finished time and do not read elapsed.
   - Otherwise read elapsed exactly once and show it.
   - If the shown value is absent, output "-:--:--" styled progress.elapsed.
   - Otherwise truncate to whole seconds, convert with the same conversion TimeRemainingColumn uses, and style with progress.elapsed.
   - Set no refresh cap. Cache nothing.
2. Capture on update. Progress update keeps its existing order. As the last step inside its lock, if completed is at least total and no finished time is present, read elapsed once and store it, even if absent.
3. Capture on advance. Progress advance applies the same rule after adding to completed and appending its sample, inside its lock. Its own time read stays before the lock.
4. Clearing. The task's internal reset clears the sample history and the finished time; Progress update calls it whenever a total is passed. Progress reset also clears the finished time explicitly before refreshing. Start, stop, and stop_task neither capture nor clear. Progress reset with completed equal to total does not capture.
5. Total change. When update receives a total, clear the finished time first, then apply completed and run the capture rule in the same call.
6. Completed lowered. Lowering completed does not clear a captured finished time.
7. Creation. add_task does not capture, even if completed is at or above total.
## Data model
- Task gains a public field finished_time: an optional number of seconds, default absent. Declare it as a plain defaulted field after the callable clock field and before the visibility flag, as in the reference. Positional callers passing the visibility flag or later fields are affected; keyword callers are not.
- Give it a short docstring like the other Task fields.
- The Task finished property becomes "a finished time is present". It stays read-only and returns a boolean.
- Consumers inherit this: the bar column's finished styling, Task.time_remaining (zero when finished), and Progress.finished.
## API contracts
- TimeElapsedColumn is a public class in the progress module, a subclass of the ProgressColumn base, exported like TimeRemainingColumn. Its constructor takes no arguments. Its render method takes a task and returns a rich Text object styled progress.elapsed.
- Task.finished_time is public, readable, and writable, with the semantics in Terminology.
- Palette.__rich__ is a public method taking only the instance and returns a rich Table:
  - Three columns in order: index, RGB, Color. Title "Palette". Caption is the number of colors followed by " colors", right-justified. Highlighting enabled.
  - One row per palette color, in palette order.
  - Index cell: the index as a plain string.
  - RGB cell: a plain string such as "(r, g, b)" of the triplet's three integers. No type name or field names.
  - Color cell: a text object of 16 spaces with a background built from the stored triplet.
## Module architecture
- The column class lives in rich/progress.py directly after the bar column and before TimeRemainingColumn. It sets no refresh cap, writes no state, reads only the public Task attributes finished, finished_time, and elapsed, and has a one-line docstring.
- The style default goes in rich/default_styles.py among the progress.* entries, with a yellow foreground.
- Palette.__rich__ lives in rich/palette.py. That module must not import table, text, style, or color modules at module level, because the color module imports the palette data at module level and that creates a cycle. Import them inside the method, and use a type-checking-only import for the table annotation.
- CHANGELOG.md gets a new unreleased section with an Added entry naming Progress.TimeElapsedColumn.
## Implementation constraints
- Clock reads are pinned by tests, because the test clock advances one unit per read:
  - Each column call performs one shared clock read in the base column call, before render logic. A finished render reads no clock. The column adds no other reads.
  - Each capture reads elapsed exactly once, only when the rule fires, and stores that value directly.
  - In update, the capture is the last clock-related step. In advance, the capture's read comes after advance's own time read.
  - Do not change the order of existing reads in update, advance, or reset.
- Use the existing lock; do not add one. Capture happens inside it, so readers never see a completed count without its captured value.
- Capture at most once until cleared. Later updates and advances must not overwrite it.
- Add no imports, packages, or configuration to rich/progress.py beyond what it already uses.
## Compatibility
- In normal progression (completed rising to total, no reset) the new finished property matches the old one. These reference behaviors must not be "fixed":
  - Lowering completed after a finish keeps the task finished.
  - An update that receives a total recaptures in the same call if completed is at or above the new total.
  - add_task or reset with completed at or above total reports unfinished until an update or advance.
## Behavioral acceptance criteria
- An unstarted task renders "-:--:--" with the progress.elapsed style.
- A started, unfinished task renders live elapsed time.
- A task reaching its total 10 seconds after starting keeps showing 0:00:10 afterward.
- Stopping a display or calling stop_task does not freeze a value. Progress reset clears it.
- By default the column text is yellow; a user theme can override it.
- The standard palette's __rich__ returns a table with 16 rows.
## Test requirements
- Add a unit test for TimeElapsedColumn in the progress test module, following the TimeRemainingColumn pattern. Drive the task through public update and advance calls with a controlled clock, never by assigning the finished time. Check unstarted, running, and finished (frozen after the clock advances) states.
- Update test_columns as one coupled change:
  - Add TimeElapsedColumn after TimeRemainingColumn in its column list, and import it with the other progress names.
  - Regenerate its expected output from the base. Change only: (a) each row gains one progress.elapsed cell, after the time-remaining cell and before the file-size cell; (b) bar widths shrink in every frame because the new column takes width; (c) clock-derived values (elapsed and speed) shifted by the extra clock reads.
  - Every other character stays byte-identical to the base, including escape sequences and padding. Do not add or drop padding by hand.
  - Derive each clock-derived value by tracing clock reads in order. A finished task's elapsed value is the value stored at its capture read and stays fixed in later frames.
  - If the test can run, run it and confirm every difference falls into category (a), (b), or (c). If it cannot, say so in the final report and cite the trace used.
- Add tests/test_palette.py with one test, test_rich_cast. It imports the module-level standard palette from rich._palettes, calls __rich__ directly with no arguments, and asserts the result is a Table with 16 rows. Do not wrap the palette in a new Palette; its constructor takes a sequence of triplets and wrapping raises an error.
- Add no new test framework or fixture library.
